thread:
sara_support: Escalation — Acme Prod (acct: acme-prod) can't reach their private Redwood inference endpoint from their app VPC. Intermittent TLS timeouts and a lot of 524/connect timeouts starting ~08:45 UTC. Works from a laptop on internet. Suspect NACL/SG egress or NATGW.

Tom_csev: Can you paste the exact error the app sees? Also which private endpoint hostname?

sara_support: They report `tls: handshake timeout` in the client logs and the app returns 504 after 30s. Hostname: `inference.acme-prod.rw-inference.private` (private VPC endpoint).

alex_infra: Quick checklist: 1) Is there a NAT Gateway or Egress-only IGW? 2) Are you using per-customer egress IPs or AWS NAT? 3) Any corporate outbound allowlist on their side?

sara_support: Customer says they use a managed NAT Gateway (nat-0a1b2c3d) + custom NACL on the private subnet. They also have an egress allowlist appliance but claim it's bypassed for this test.

jen_oncall: Can we get a traceroute / curl from a host in the same subnet? Also tcpdump showing the SYNs would be ideal.

sara_support: Customer ran these from one of their app nodes. Pasted output: ```
$ curl -v --max-time 10 https://inference.acme-prod.rw-inference.private/health
* About to connect() to inference.acme-prod.rw-inference.private port 443 (#0)
* Trying 10.0.5.23...
* connect to 10.0.5.23 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to inference.acme-prod.rw-inference.private port 443: Connection timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 10001 milliseconds
```

alex_infra: That IP 10.0.5.23 looks like the private ENI we gave them for the private endpoint. Timeout suggests packets leave the instance but no return. Do they have a stateful SG or stateless NACL blocking ephemeral replies?

tom_csev: Customer ran `nc -vz 10.0.5.23 443` and got `Connection timed out`. They also ran `telnet 10.0.5.23 443` same. They did a `traceroute -n 10.0.5.23` and it stops at the NAT hop.

jen_oncall: Ask them for a tcpdump on the app node while replicating: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.0.5.23 and tcp port 443 and '(tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0)' -w /tmp/syn.pcap` — we want to see SYNs and any SYN/ACK.

sara_support: Customer uploaded pcap. I checked: there are SYNs out to the NAT IP but no SYN/ACKs returned. I also see correct source ports in 32768-33000 range.

alex_infra: Classic NACL issue: if NACL has inbound rules that don't allow ephemeral ports back to the instance (return traffic from the endpoint comes from 443 to ephemeral port), then the responses get dropped. NACLs are stateless so you must allow both directions. Request they check NACL rules for the private subnet and ensure ephemeral range (1024-65535 or at least 32768-61000) is allowed inbound AND outbound.

sara_support: Asked customer to paste NACL entries. They had ALLOW 443 outbound -> 0.0.0.0/0 but no inbound rule allowing ephemeral. Inbound rules only allowed 443 from a narrow IP set.

tom_csev: That would block the return SYN/ACKs because the source port on the response is 443 and destination is ephemeral. NACL inbound sees destination ephemeral port and denies. Ask them to temporarily insert an ALLOW inbound rule for ephemeral ports from the Redwood egress CIDR we gave them for testing (we previously gave `34.120.16.0/20, 35.190.0.0/16` as example egress ranges).

sara_support: Customer applied temp NACL rule: inbound ALLOW TCP 32768-65535 from 34.120.16.0/20 and outbound ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 to 34.120.16.0/20.

netscan-bot: scan result — after change, 443 reachable: `tcp open` from host 10.0.6.12 -> 10.0.5.23:443.

sara_support: Customer re-ran `curl` and now shows TLS handshake proceeding and 200 OK.

jen_oncall: Good. For long-term: (1) add ephemeral port ranges to the NACL for the subnet, (2) prefer stateful SG rules (if possible) so return traffic is automatic, (3) consider using our dedicated egress IP option if they have strict allowlists. Also check if they have an intermediate firewall appliance doing port-based inspection that might rewrite source ports.

alex_infra: Also remind them that NACLs are ordered — make sure the ALLOW entry has a lower rule number than a DENY that might be matching 0.0.0.0/0.

sara_support: Customer will keep the temp allow rule and schedule a maintenance window to harden. They're going to convert the subnet to use SG-centric controls where possible. Marking this escalated ticket as resolved by customer. :white_check_mark:

jen_oncall: Closing notes: root cause = stateless NACL blocking ephemeral return ports to app nodes; symptom = TLS handshake timeout/connect timeouts to private inference ENI. Remediation steps and permanent recommendations posted.

sara_support: Will file a KB with the steps and add an internal note to include ephemeral port guidance in our onboarding docs for Private deployments.
